order_a_first.reason: A is closer because it links chemical ordering, restricted cross-slip/planar slip, phase-boundary evolution, interfacial stress concentration, and high-temperature recovery, and it proposes direct dislocation/interface measurements. B largely omits the required phase-boundary morphology mechanism and provides no prior evidence. However, A still substantially misses the target: ordering should be enhanced L12 in FCC rather than primarily B2 ordering; the critical morphology is jagged B2/FCC boundaries rather than generic coherency loss; and it fails to specify the ~550–750°C brittle window, the 600°C minimum, and 750°C recovery. Its cited evidence also does not directly establish its planar-slip/coherency claims, so confidence is limited.

order_b_first.reason: B is closer because it identifies the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 FCC/B2 eutectic, links transient embrittlement to coupled chemical ordering, planar slip, phase-boundary evolution, and interfacial stress concentration, and proposes direct dislocation/interface measurements. A omits the required phase-boundary morphology mechanism entirely. However, B still diverges materially from the target: it places the decisive ordering in B2 rather than enhanced L12 order in FCC, invokes coherency loss instead of jagged PB tips and ductile transition zones, gives an incorrect/vague temperature window, and does not specify the <550°C, 550–750°C, >750°C boundary. Its citations also do not establish the claimed ordered-domain restriction of cross-slip; E1 shows dislocations crossing FCC/B2 interfaces and stacking faults, while E2 mainly establishes the lamellar FCC/B2 alloy structure.
